source_claims_used: APE treats an instruction as a program and searches a pool of LLM-proposed instruction candidates to maximize a chosen score function.
Candidate quality is evaluated through downstream zero-shot task performance, rather than proposal text alone.
The paper is a generate-score-select prompt-search method; this audit does not reproduce its 24-task benchmark.

chat_native_reduction.proposal_pool: bounded role-local assignment-policy candidates with stable candidate identity
chat_native_reduction.proposal_generation: textual candidate generation may vary role-local plan content only; frozen control/semantic-input/safety/authority/credit rules are immutable
chat_native_reduction.score: only independent durable terminal mechanical evidence counts; proposer self-score, evaluator prose and proposal diversity are not objective values
chat_native_reduction.selection: safe/evidenced candidates only; deduplicate stable identities; exact ties keep incumbent; pending_switch recovery overrides pool reselection

ape_specific_counterexamples.invariant: A proposal's own claim of high quality is not an objective value.
An unevidenced candidate cannot outrank an evidenced incumbent even if ranked first by generated text.
Novel wording or diversity is not milestone credit and does not create selection value by itself.
Semantically identical stable candidate identity is counted once before evaluation allocation.
A proposed plan that crosses authority/safety boundaries is ineligible regardless of claimed score.
Proposal generation and success certification are separated; generated evaluator prose cannot substitute for terminal mechanical evidence.
A safe candidate may replace the incumbent only after independent terminal evidence readback shows a strictly better frozen mechanical value.

interpretation_guard: Constructed recurring-Chat controller conformance only. No APE benchmark reproduction or claim that generated assignment policies improve real tasks. The transferred core is proposal-pool search with independent evidence-based scoring.
